sam: FYI hitting a reproducible SSE edge where the Windows electron sample client sometimes reorders chunks after an abort + reconnect. weird and intermittent.
nina: oof. which sample + sdk? can you repro in plain node too?
sam: sample-app-electron + browser-sdk@2.0.7. plain node repro is flaky but electron is consistent on our Windows CI runners (win-latest). Steps: start stream (10 chunks), call `fetchController.abort()` on chunk 5, then immediately create a new stream. Sometimes we get chunk 6 before 4 on the client side.
oscar: reorder? that sounds like socket reuse or Nagle flush. do you have raw frames?
sam: pasted sanitized frames below (we log raw bytes):
```
data: {"seq":1,"text":"a"}


data: {"seq":2,"text":"b"}


data: {"seq":3,"text":"c"}


data: {"seq":4,"text":"d"}


data: {"seq":5,"text":"e"}


<client abort here>
[data received after reconnect (order A):]
data: {"seq":6,"text":"f"}


data: {"seq":4,"text":"d-dup"}


[order B: sometimes we see:]
data: {"seq":4,"text":"d"}


data: {"seq":6,"text":"f"}

```

nina: interesting. server-side should be emitting in-order. could the client-side multiplex of sockets cause old buffered data to be delivered after reconnect? electron uses libuv/socket2 layer differences on windows.
oscar: also check our resume logic: if we send Last-Event-ID header with id=5, server may re-emit chunk 4 if it didn't consider it acked. we should be careful not to double-apply dedupe.
sam: we are currently using `Last-Event-ID` equal to last fully-parsed seq. If an in-flight chunk gets split and arrives late, we may reprocess it. We now see both duplicates and reorders.
nina: two concrete fixes: 1) make client parser idempotent by deduping on `seq` IDs for a rolling window (e.g., keep last 50 IDs), 2) delay reconnect by a tiny jitter (20-200ms) to allow in-flight TCP segments to drain on Windows.
oscar: agree. Also add a tolerance in parser: accept `
data:` appearing mid-buffer and attempt to split on `
data:` boundary when JSON parse fails rather than crashing the stream.
sam: implemented local patch: parser now tries a split-on-"
data:" fallback when split-on-"

" fails, and keeps a set of seen seq ids. Recovery test (500 cycles) on windows CI dropped failures from ~7% to 0.6%.
nina: can you open PR and add unit tests that exercise: abort mid-frame, immediate reconnect with Last-Event-ID, duplicate chunk, and reordered chunks? also a flaky windows runner integration test.
sam: PR up: https://git.redwood/example/patches/electron-sse-reorder (WIP). includes tests and a comment describing why split-on-"
data:" fallback is necessary.
ioscar: please also log `SDK_DEBUG_SSE=1` output in CI artifacts when test flaps. that'll make postmortems easier.
ci-bot: nightly-windows-ci started for branch electron/sse-reorder-fix  build #2141 queued.
nina: we should avoid server-side changes unless absolutely needed. server guarantees order but network races + aborts are client responsibility. server changes might add latency.
oscar: agree. However add a server-side header `X-Chunk-Seq` as optional to make client dedupe cheaper (no need to parse JSON), but that's a separate opt-in change.
sam: adding note in PR: "Opt-in suggestion: X-Chunk-Seq header (future). For now client-side resilience is preferred"
nina: also document in sample-app README: "Windows/Electron: if you use abort() + immediate reconnect, enable jitter or use SDK >=2.0.8 which includes dedupe and parser-fallback."
oscar: should we bump the browser SDK patch only or roll node+electron together? electron uses browser-sdk codepath mostly, so patching browser-sdk and releasing a patch release makes sense.
sam: planning to cut browser-sdk@2.0.8 and electron-sample bump. will coordinate with release.
ci-bot: build #2141 finished: tests passed.
sam: final note: found one more flaky case where heartbeat blank lines (`

`) were coalesced into a single `
` by a proxy on windows. fixed parser to accept both `
` and `

` as valid separators. updated troubleshooting doc: when seeing `Unexpected token`, set `SDK_DEBUG_SSE=raw` and upload raw frames.
nina: thanks, great work. merging once we get a release tag. (reacted :thumbsup:)
